messages:
jin (eng-ml): Heads up — we're onboarding a new model from Gladius called 'NightBloom-7B'. LicenseScan attached. It looks like: research-only, mandatory UI attribution, and an explicit 'no redistribution of weights' clause. Can legal/infra confirm whether we can: (a) run hosted inference for paying customers, (b) run quantized derivatives for evaluation, or (c) include this in Dedicated/Private offers?

maria (legal): tagging @owen @sara. Short answer: 'research-only' typically prohibits commercial use, so running a paid hosted endpoint would be a problem. Redistribution ban would block shipping quantized weight files. Attribution is doable but doesn't override the research-only restriction. Need the full license text and vendor confirmation.

jin (eng-ml): Pasted excerpt from the license we received: ```
LICENSE: Gladius Research Model License v1.2
- Permitted: research and internal evaluation.
- Prohibited: commercial exploitation (including paid hosting or API access) without separate agreement.
- Attribution: "Model: NightBloom-7B (Gladius Research)" must be displayed where outputs are surfaced.
- Redistribution: weights and derivative model files may not be redistributed or shipped.
```
Also there's a line that reads: "Derivative representations for benchmarking/evaluation permitted under non-distribution, ephemeral use only."

liz (eng-ml): For quant experiments we normally produce q4_0 artifacts that we persist to S3 for reproducibility. If redistribution is banned, can we at least run quantized in-memory for evals and then delete everything?

maria (legal): Running inference in a hosted, paid product is likely commercial use. If customers pay for the endpoint, that triggers the prohibition unless we get a commercial license. Regarding quantization: if we generate artifacts and they remain under our control but are used to serve customers, that may still be treated as redistribution/derivative distribution depending on wording. Ephemeral in-memory quantization for internal evaluation is safer.

license-bot: license-scan: flags -> research-only, no-redistribution, attribution-required, no-obvious-export-control-clauses-detected (vendor contact recommended).

owen (compliance): Also flag jurisdiction/export controls. Gladius is EU-based but model provenance unknown. Ask them whether there are any export restrictions or third-party data-origin clauses. Also clarify whether the attribution can be in logs only or must be visible in the UI shown to end users.

sara (platform): Technically we can implement a "no-export" guard: run quantization with tmpfs or /dev/shm, revoke S3 write permissions in the task role, and ensure derived files never hit long-term storage. For hosted/Dedicated differences: Dedicated (our reserved infra) still counts as our service unless the customer brings their own model (BYOM) and manages it in Private.

maria (legal): Correct — if the customer provides their own model (BYOM) and hosts it on Private under their control, we are not redistributing. If we perform quantization and keep artifacts in our environment, that could be considered creating derivatives we control. We should ask Gladius for a written waiver or a commercial sublicense if we want to offer Hosted/Dedicated endpoints to customers.

liz (eng-ml): Quick question: the license allows "derivative representations for benchmarking/evaluation permitted under non-distribution, ephemeral use only" — does that let us run in-memory evals for onboarding and store metrics?

maria (legal): Storing evaluation metrics is fine. "Evaluation" typically covers internal benchmarks and model quality checks. It does not cover providing a paid inference API. Keep any derived model files ephemeral, log the commands and evidence of deletion. We should retain audit logs showing artifacts were transient.

jin (eng-ml): OK — proposed action items: 1) @liz run eval-only quant runs with strict ephemeral policy (no S3 writes) and attach logs to the onboarding ticket; 2) @sara draft the technical controls (no-export guard) and a checklist for the onboarding PR; 3) @maria to request a commercial license/hosting waiver from Gladius and confirm attribution semantics; 4) pause any Hosted/Dedicated rollout until legal says ok. React with :thumbsup: if that works.

sara (platform): I'll sketch the guard. Quick design note: mount tmpfs at /mnt/nightbloom, disable instance role S3 PutObject for the task, set NIGHTBLOOM_EPHEMERAL=1 env var, and add an infra-test that verifies no model files are present in S3 after job completes. I'll open a draft RFC.

liz (eng-ml): Starting eval now using an in-memory quant path: `./tools/quantize --mode inmem --model-dir /mnt/nightbloom --out /dev/shm/nightbloom_q4 --keep-logs /tmp/nightbloom_eval.log` — I'll attach /tmp/nightbloom_eval.log to the ticket and then rm -rf the /dev/shm file and record the deletion timestamp.

maria (legal): Also capture the vendor contact email and the exact license file you received. We need to send a short note: "Please confirm in writing whether providing inference as a paid service is permitted under the license, and whether you can grant a hosting sublicense or waiver for dedicated customers." If they refuse, we need to drop NightBloom from Hosted onboarding.

jin (eng-ml): Thanks — marking onboarding status: blocked. I'll create the vendor follow-up and link it here. If Gladius replies confirming commercial hosting is allowed with attribution, we can re-open.

license-bot: ticket-created -> #onboard-1739 (vendor: gladius@vendor.example.com).
